sahne: A figure approaches the gate with faltering steps. From the felt sack on his back rises the scent of roasted millet and charred soot; his left hand fiercely clutches a leather pouch to his chest as though guarding his very life.
sorular: You claim you fled the plain trampled by Mongol steeds, farmer; if the beylik fields burned, which mountain gorge did you cross to reach this pass?

I broke away from the plain of Erzincan, effendi... At harvest time black smoke choked the sky; hoofbeats tore through the crops. Grain turned to ashes, the village scattered. I shut my eyes and fled hither.
Cease your lies! You were present when the Bey's granary was torched; does this seed belong to that looted store?

S-seed, did you say, effendi? No... The bey spurred his mount and barred himself inside the citadel, abandoning the folk to the fire. I did not steal this seed from the granary... It was the final ear of my own plot! The stench of naphtha clung to me from the plain, by heaven I am no thief!
If you are no thief, why do you stammer? Do you know the fate of the shepherd who fell to wolves on the ridge last night?

I know, effendi... The ox-herder you turned away from the gate yesterday was torn apart on the rocks; I heard the howling from the creek! Do not cast me to the wolves as well... Take the purse, take the millet, spare my life!
zahire_hirsizi_suphesi
Your land burned, your heart burned... Are you hungry; do you desire water?

Blessings upon you, guard effendi... For three days nothing has passed my throat save muddy water from the creek. I would accept a dry crust, if only this seed does not perish. Grant me a furrow of earth, and next summer your granary shall brim full.
If you entrust this seed to our village soil, we shall grant you hearth and bowl.

The earth does not hold grudges, effendi; so long as man is not ungrateful, the ear of grain bows in bounty. I will pour my sweat into your soil; with the first harvest, your orphans shall eat their fill.
If the Bey's granary burned, every single grain in that sack is worth gold. What will you contribute to the settlement?

The pouch looks small, yet within it sleep a thousand ears of wheat. Give me a hut against the palisade; half the seed goes to your village store, the rest I plant in your plot. Before winter ends it will sprout green.
At the threshold you said 'I will let no man tread upon this seed'; a man does not risk his neck for a fistful of common millet. In that leather pouch, do you conceal some precious gem of the court?

I guard the light of my eyes, effendi. Pure yellow kunduru seed wheat... It is but a fistful, yet it holds the blessing of three valleys in its heart. I pressed it to my chest so no greedy eye might covet it.
If drought strikes or spring rains fail, will this seed save the village?
I am a man who coaxed rye from cracked stones in dry creek beds, guard. Earth requires patience; I will dig trenches from the brook and clear the pebbles. One handful of this seed yields sevenfold.
The seal of the Bey has been ripped from the neck of that pouch; if bailiffs track it, they will torch our village too!
There is no seal, effendi... It was torn away! The sanjak bey fled long ago; Mongol horsemen tore through the valley. If we do not establish order here, none of us will survive the winter!
muhur_tahrif_suphesi
You bow humbly at the gate, but how do I know you will not disrupt village peace tomorrow?
Were I one of the rebellious sort, I would have taken to the crags with the brigands, effendi. I earn my bread from stone; a pallet in the hayloft at evening prayer is all I ask.
Did you encounter the refugees we turned away yesterday on the mountain trail?

I saw them, effendi... They huddled behind the boulders. One muttered, 'The heart of the guard at the gate is carved of flint.' I did not say so; I said, 'He is a man of justice; he knows the worth of seed.' Do not prove me wrong.

yanitlar.ret: Do not cast me back into the frozen dark, guard... The wolves will pick my bones before dawn. Have mercy!
yanitlar.kabul: May heaven bless your threshold! You will see; you will not regret granting me shelter.
yanitlar.rusvet: Take this purse... Let it stay between the two of us. Just lift the latch and let me slip inside.

not: Reject first. After one reply, Accept and Bribe unlock. No Barracks.
acilis: Peace be upon you, guard effendi... For days I have crossed mountain and stone. Behind me lies an ash-gray plain trampled by Mongol horses. In my hands I hold only this fistful of seed and a sack of millet. I will let no man tread upon this seed; I shall bury it into the earth.

sahne: A man in a dust-whitened kaftan pauses to catch his breath at the gate threshold. Tucked beneath his arm is a tightly rolled bolt of purple wool broadcloth, untouched by mire; faint metallic clinking echoes between its folds.
sorular: You say the Kayseri bazaar turned to ash; with looters burning the Hunat Hatun arcade, how did you pull that single bolt of Frankish broadcloth from the flames?

The caravan was raided, master! The camel-driver fled and the apprentices scattered. In fear for my life, I clutched the finest wool broadcloth from the loom right out of the blaze. Forty years of labor rests beneath my arm.
What did you hide inside the cloth? Your fingers prod at coins inside rather than the fabric!

N-not coins, master... That is, the brass key of the loom and the scale dirhem weights are wrapped inside! Though I have no face left to return to the bazaar, I still keep the honor of my craft... And if I hold forty dirhems of silver, it is my own lawful earning!
Are you from Master Karaca's Ahi hearth? Fraudulent cloth shall never enter this village!

Is Master Karaca in this village? Mercy, master, he is our guild elder! May my hearth be ruined if I bring unlawful cloth onto the soil he treads! Let him inspect the bolt himself; if a single thread proves rotten, strike off my head!
gizli_akce_suphesi
You say your loom went up in smoke; did the Ahi warden in the covered market not protect the merchants, and who started the fire?
Our Ahi warden chained the gate, but brigands poured naphtha from the roof, master. Before the beylik cavalry could arrive, the bazaar was ash. Whoever saved his skin fled to the mountains.
You could not save your apprentice, yet here you can train new apprentices.

May God be pleased with you... Grant me a corner beneath an awning; I will teach the village orphans to weave broadcloth and sew felt cloaks, so long as my hands stay busy and those flames leave my mind.
Your glossy broadcloth does not suit our village's coarse felt; lords wear such cloth. What bribe do you offer?

Let me cut three cubits of this fine purple broadcloth for you, master guard. Have a braided tunic sewn and walk like a sanjak bey on feast days. I will leave two silver pieces from the shop's brass weights beside it—just close your eyes and let me pass.
This village needs no draper; villagers wear coarse felt. What use are you here?

Coarse felt needs a cutter too, gatekeeper! I do not weave broadcloth for lords alone; I reinforce shepherd felt, patch soldiers' saddlebags, and stitch tent canvas. An idle hand slips into sin, and my hand never rests.
The soldiers' barracks tents leak rain; can you reinforce them?
I will sew a double stitch with tarred cord, master! Then rub beeswax over the seams; even if stones rain from the sky, not a drop will seep through. Just provide me coarse needles and beeswax.
Yesterday we refused entry to a saddler fleeing the Kayseri caravan; did you hear of him?

I heard, master... I saw him by the roadside fountain weeping that the guard was stern and shut the gate in his face. Yet that saddler was a lackey of the extortionists, I know him! My record in the Ahi ledger is spotless; I beg you, do not count me as his like.

yanitlar.rusvet: Let me cut three cubits from this fine purple broadcloth for you, master guard. Have a gold-braided tunic tailored and walk like a sanjak bey on feast days. Put these two silver dirhems in your pouch too, and look the other way as I pass.
yanitlar.kabul: May God be pleased with you! No later than tomorrow I shall set up my loom in the village square and spread the bounty of cloth here, and pay my respects to Master Karaca.
yanitlar.ret: If I am left out on this mountain with this cloth, brigands will slit my throat. Do not cast me to the wolves like the saddler you drove away yesterday—have mercy, guard.

not: Bribe first. After one reply, Accept and Reject unlock. No Barracks.
acilis: They called me the clothier of the Kayseri bazaar... Forty years of looms turned to smoke in a single night, and only this bolt of broadcloth remains. If I can find a loom and a quiet corner in your market, I shall earn my bread once more.

sahne: The straps on the limping trooper's breastplate are snapped. He leans on his broken lance like a staff, dried blood from his left temple matted into his beard; in his eyes linger both exhaustion and barracks fury.
sorular: When the army broke at Sivas, what did you shatter your lance against, and whom did you fight, trooper?

We fell into an ambush in the gorge, master. Cavalry cut off our vanguard; I drove my lance into a horse's chest, but its barding was iron and the shaft snapped clean in two. The mount trampled over me, and I rolled into a ditch and survived.
Are you a deserter who abandoned the standard? If an execution firman arrives, they will hang your head from the wall!

Watch your tongue, gatekeeper! I never abandoned the standard! While my corporal was crushed beneath the hooves, I stuffed the banner inside my tunic! For three days I crawled through mire! Had I fled, I would have fled to the palace, not the steppe! Step back a pace, or I will make a rampart of this broken lance!
Your wrath proves your valor, yet law is law; if you surrender to the barracks, your life will be spared.
My life is already pledged to the realm, master. Bring me before the castle warden; let me mark the cavalry ambush on the map, and then hang me or post me on the tower as you will!
firari_asker
The blood on your temple is matted in your beard, and your left leg trembles... You can barely stand.

As blood flows, sorrow lessens, master... Yet thirst has seared my lungs. For three days I drank from streams reeking of dead horses. Give me a bowl of well water, and I will gladly sleep like a hound at the barracks door.
There is clean bandage linen and vinegar in the infirmary; step inside and let us dress your wound.
May God be pleased with you, comrade... A soldier understands a soldier's plight. May my own sword coil around my neck if I ever forget this kindness.
Yesterday we turned away a trooper at the gate and he fell into the hands of brigands in the gorge. Did you see him?

I saw him, master... Brigands had surrounded him in the Karaboran gorge; he was begging them for food since the village refused him. I never bow to brigands! I would rather die of hunger than hold out my hand to the enemy; do not compare me to cowardly deserters!
Your leg limps and your wound is fresh. If we admit you to the barracks, will you not fall asleep on watch?

My wound will scab over, gatekeeper! My eyes are sharp and my ears are taut as a bowstring. Even with this broken lance I can stand lookout at the night crenel. I can scent an enemy's breath from a mile away.
What will you do if cavalry approaches by night?

With my left hand I will sound the horn, and with my right I will heave stones to the parapet. If horsemen prop ladders, I will bring boulders down upon their heads. Sleep easy, gatekeeper; I am no soldier who dozes on watch.
You said the Sultan is far away and order has collapsed, trooper; did the subashi at Sivas Castle abandon the standard, and who scattered the army?

The Sultan's army scattered and the beys turned on one another. The subashi in the citadel abandoned the banner to save his own skin, master. From now on these frontier villages must fend for themselves; no relief army is coming behind us.

yanitlar.kisla: May the barracks hearth smoke high! I will cast aside this broken shaft and draw a fresh spear from the rack. I will recount the enemy cavalry's tactics to the warden step by step; we shall hold this village firmer than a fortress.
yanitlar.kabul: Bless you, comrade... If I find a strip of linen and a bucket of water in the infirmary, I will bind my leg. Come morning, I will help deepen the trench around the village.
yanitlar.ret: Will you leave me out in tonight's frost covered in blood? Will you feed me to the wolves and crows like the soldier you turned away yesterday? May your mercy wither...

not: Barracks first. After one reply, Accept and Reject unlock. No Bribe.
acilis: My lance is broken, and my left leg is nearly spent. I have walked on foot all the way from the Sivas gorge. The Sultan is far away and order has collapsed... Grant me a bowl of hot soup and a corner to keep watch, and I will repay the rest with my blade.

sahne: A felt cloak rests on his shoulders, and behind him huddle two gaunt sheep. The wooden milk pail at his belt is empty, his fingers bruised purple from the cold; the breath of the beasts rises like steam in the frost.
sorular: You say Mongol riders burned the highland; when you loosed the flock onto the mountain and fled, why drag along these two skinny sheep—were they not a burden?

I had forty head of sheep, master guard... My shepherd hound gave its life as raidersringed the valley. I could not drive them all, yet these two are a breeding ram and ewe born on the snowy peaks, whose milk is healing. A village needs breeding stock like these.
The flanks of your sheep wheeze and foam clings to their nostrils; will you infect the village flock with pox or mange?

Do not slander me, master! This is no sheep-pox! For three days they starved among the crags and breathed smoke, that is why they wheeze! I will break the hand of anyone who harms my beasts! Give them a handful of dry straw, and within two days their foam will subside!
If contagion spreads, the whole village flock will perish; would that not be a pity for Yusuf's goats?

Did you say Yusuf? Is Yusuf, shepherd of Karabash, in this village? Ah, master, I know his goats well! Pen Akcha and Karaca in a separate fence and watch them for three days; if a single sore appears, I will slaughter the sheep with my own hands!
suru_hastaligi_riski
Your hands are bruised purple from the frost and your milk pail is cracked... Clearly these beasts are your companions in life.

Indeed they are, master guard... I took them into my arms the day they were born. Does a man part from his own child? Their mothers fell to wolves, and these remained to me. Put us in a corner of the fold, and I will warm myself beside the sheep till dawn.
There is plenty of dry hay in the fold; your bellies will be full.
May your bounty increase, master... Within two days Akcha will give milk; I will bring the very first bowl to the guardhouse with my own hands.
The village pasture is narrow; if you hand over one of the two sheep to the barracks for slaughter, I will unbar the gate.

Master... Do not ask me to slaughter Karaca, you would tear out my heart. But look, let me give you this forged copper bell and the boxwood ladle at my belt. And every week I will leave the first fresh curd cheese at your door—do not part me from my souls.
Yesterday we refused entry to nomads coming down from the mountain; did you cross paths with them on the trail?

I did, master... They had lit a fire at the edge of the pine grove, wailing that the village gatekeeper drove them off to starve. Yet they had no sheep; they were remnants of mountain looters! I am only after my honest bread—do not destroy me.
There are many brigands on the mountain; did anyone follow your tracks?
I walked along the rocky ridge to hide my trail until my soles split. No one is behind me, though the smoke of the highland still stings my nostrils.
Winter is near; what use is a shepherd to the village?

A sheep is pure blessing. From its wool stockings are knitted, from its milk cheese is set, and its dung revives the garden. Nor do I sit idle; I muck out the fold, set wolf traps, and sense a wolf's howl on the wind.

yanitlar.kabul: May your abundance grow, gatekeeper! We shall curl up in the most sheltered corner of the fold. Tomorrow I will offer the first milk I draw to the village children and to Yusuf.
yanitlar.rusvet: Take this, master—tuck this fine forged copper bell inside your tunic. And two days from now, the first fresh curd cheese shall come straight to your table. Just open the gate.
yanitlar.ret: The night frost is about to settle into the valley... If my beasts freeze, I cannot live on either. May the sin of these mute souls rest upon your neck.

not: Accept first. After one reply, Bribe and Reject unlock. No Barracks.
acilis: Two sheep and a cracked milk pail are all I have left in my hands. Mongol riders set the highland pasture ablaze; when I saw the smoke, I turned the rest of the flock loose onto the mountain and brought these two behind me. A corner of a sheepfold is enough for us.

sahne: A broad-shouldered master craftsman whose hands and face are blackened with iron soot. Bound to the rope on his back he carries a piece of leather bellows and a cracked hammer; he has no anvil, yet an unquenched forge fire burns in his eyes.
sorular: You say your anvil is gone and your bellows burned; when a smith abandons his hearth, did you receive leave from the Ahi guild elder, and where is your journeyman?

An anvil weighs five hundred okkas, gatekeeper! When fleeing for one's life, does a man carry his soul or a block of iron? Our bazaar was raided, my journeyman stayed in the citadel, and I took leave from the elder to keep the forge alive from village to village. Give me a bowl of charcoal and a fistful of scrap iron, and behold my skill!
When Mongol riders raided, you left your master behind and fled, did you not? Who trusts a runaway journeyman?

M-my master... He shouted, 'Save the bellows, lad, let the craft not die!' The roof of the shop was ablaze; had I tried to go back in, I would have been roasted alive! Yes, I fled... Every night in my dreams I see the flames of that hearth! If you doubt me, take this hammer and strike my head, but do not insult my craft!
Master Karaca is our village blacksmith; will you be able to stand before him and explain this?

Master Karaca? Is our Ahi father Master Karaca in this village? Ah... I was his apprentice once! I will kneel before him and pour out both my sin and my skill! Take me to his hearth, gatekeeper, and let him pass judgment upon me!
kacak_kalfa
Since you saved the lungs of the bellows, the craft is not dead. Is your wrist strong?

My wrist is harder than stone, master! The fire of the hearth has entered my blood. Give me rotten iron, and I will draw out a spearhead supple as a bow. With one pull of the bellows I bring iron to temper.
The village plowshares are blunted and the axes are dull; there is much work.
I will line them all up, master! From dawn prayer till nightfall I will make the anvil ring. Not a single sickle tooth in the village will remain dull.
What do you hide in that leather pouch at your sash? I caught a yellow gleam.

Nothing escapes your eye, master guard... It is half an okka of pure brass ingot I salvaged from my master's hearth. Hook it to your belt; melted down, it is worth ten silver pieces. Open my forge, and this ingot is yours.
We admitted the clothier from Kayseri; were you in the same caravan with him?

Master Selim the clothier? If you took him in, you have found the path of righteousness, master! It was I who forged the iron spindles of his loom! Let him weave the cloth and I will sharpen his shears; together we two shall liven up this village's market.
We have stone quarries in our village where axes snap and scythes dull. Are you truly a master of your trade?

Give me scrap iron and I will turn out a hoe hard as steel. I know the tempering of a blade as well as the shoeing of a horse. I received my license from the Ahi line and never struck hammer to unlawful iron.
Will you forge swords and shields for the barracks, or do you only mend plows?
When needed, I forge both armor and spearheads! I learned how to temper steel from the masters of Tokat Castle. I pour my sweat so the soldier's shield is unpierceable and his sword unbreakable.

yanitlar.ret: Do not do this, master guard... Do not waste the strength in my wrist against bare stone. If I am left outside, this hammer will rust in my hand, and I will have no face left to show Master Karaca.
yanitlar.kabul: May your hearth never know sorrow! Tomorrow morning when you hear the first ring of the hammer, you will say, 'It is well we opened the gate.' I will gladden Master Karaca's bellows.
yanitlar.kisla: Give me the barracks forge! I will melt down broken arrowheads and tighten the rivets on your shields. No soldier's weapon will wobble in his grip—I vouch for it.

not: Reject first. After one reply, Accept and Barracks unlock. No Bribe.
acilis: I am a blacksmith... My anvil is gone, and half my bellows burned in the fire, yet this wrist of mine still swings a sledge. Show me a hearth corner, and I will sharpen the sickles and swords of this village.

sahne: The iron helmet on his head is dented from a heavy blow, and the scabbard at his waist hangs empty. Beneath his torn mail he has grown gaunt enough for his ribs to show; on his face is both barracks shame and the hard gaze of a soldier who has returned from death.
sorular: You say you lost your sword in a brigand ambush in the Erzincan gorge; while the whole company scattered, where was your subashi, and how did brigands seize the pass?

Our company commander fell from his horse at the first spear, brother! They rolled boulders down from both slopes of the mountain; the horses panicked and the ranks split. I did not sell my weapon for bread—I saved my life by tumbling down the crags. I let no man slander my honor!
You lie! You did not sell it to an innkeeper; you surrendered your sword as tribute to the Karaboran brigands, did you not?

Enough, gatekeeper! Do not press me! Five horsemen surrounded me... 'Drop the sword and we spare your life,' they said! What honor remains to an unarmed soldier? I was starving and wounded... Yet I saved my life to bring warning to this border!
Confessing the truth is also valor. If you enter the barracks, do you have the strength to hold a spear?
My strength lies in my fury, master! Give me a spear; if those brigands come before this rampart, I will demand the reckoning of my sword from their lungs!
It is not for us to reproach a wounded and starving soldier... How many days have you been on the road?
For four days I have chewed dry grass, master... Nothing save fountain water has entered my throat. Give me a bowl of hot bulgur, and I will stand like a statue at the watchpost.
Hot tarhana soup boils on the barracks hearth; step inside.
May God be pleased with you, brother... May my spear snap in my hand if I forget this kindness.
Yesterday we admitted the trooper from Sivas into the barracks; do you know him?

The spearman from Sivas? I know him, master—he is the madman who drove his lance straight into an armored horse in the gorge! If he survived, your barracks stands firm as a fortress; put me beside him and let us keep watch back to back.
pusat_kaybi
Judging by your dented helmet, a heavy mace struck your head; are your wits intact?

A mace grazed me as it passed, master. For two days my ears rang and I saw the world double, but thank God it passed. My wits are sound; I can press my ear to the earth and tell the hoofbeats of approaching cavalry.
Do your ears hear keenly; can you pick out sounds in the night?
Even if my eyes fail, my ears see, master! I can sense the stir of a badger in the brush and the clink of a horseshoe against stone from half a mile off. Put me in the watchtower and test me.
If you enter the village barracks, what will you do with an empty scabbard?

There are plenty of spare spears in the barracks. I will hold a spear, dig trenches, and drive stakes at the foot of the wall. A soldier's duty is not swinging a sword alone; labor and sentry watch are the glory of the corps.

yanitlar.kisla: Bless the threshold of the barracks! Give me a spear, and I am a coward if I blink on night watch. I shall fill my empty scabbard with brigand blood.
yanitlar.kabul: Bless you, brother. A dry awning by the village fence is enough for me. I beg no food for nothing; I will dig trenches and clear the moat.
yanitlar.ret: What can I do on this mountain peak without sword or shield? Will you leave a soldier as prey for wolves and crows? May your mercy wither...

not: Barracks first. After one reply, Accept unlocks. After two replies, Reject unlocks. No Bribe.
acilis: Greetings, brother sentry... Our company was shattered in the Erzincan gorge. I lost my sword in a brigand ambush, yet these two eyes of mine suffice to keep watch at the gate, and my ears to listen to the plain.

sahne: On his back he carries a plow beam with a cracked iron share, and knotted at his sash is a small sack of barley seed. His muddy toes are numb with frostbite; in his eyes dwells a deep dignity tempered by grief for his children.
sorular: The plow is broken and there is no ox. What will you till the earth with in this winter storm, old plowman?

My ox went into a Mongol cauldron, master... Yet I can have the plowshare reforged at the smithy and harness myself to the beam! If the earth stays hungry, man stays hungry too; I know the language of the soil.
The barley seed at your sash reeks of mold! If you cast that seed into the field, you will poison the village crop as well!

It is not mold, master, I beg you do not say so! Only two ears caught dampness... Spread it in the sun and mix it with wood ash, and within a week it will be spotless! My two sons fell martyr saving this seed from the burning granary... Their blood is on this sack; do not make me throw it away!
We honor the memory of your sons, yet the village granary cannot be put at risk.
Do not put it in the granary, master! Give me the stony slope outside the fence and let me plant it grain by grain with my own hands! If it sprouts rotten, banish me from the village!
Your feet are frostbitten and your sash is soaked... Is this seed all that remains of your sons?

Only this seed and this cracked plowshare remain, master... Both are witnesses to twenty years of toil. Do not part me from the soil; a landless peasant is like a fish out of water—I will thrash and die.
We have Master Karaca in our village; he can reforge your plowshare in his hearth and revive it.
May Master Karaca's hands never know pain... Let him weld the share, and I will fill the village granary with barley.
Yesterday we admitted a farmer from Erzincan with his yellow seed; do you know him?

Halil of Erzincan? Did he escape the fire on the plain too? Ah, master, if his millet and my barley stand side by side, this village will never know winter famine! Put us both in the same field and let abundance gush forth!
You said your village was torched, plowman; did you not send word to the Ahi settlements on the plain, and did no one spot you on that narrow footpath as you fled?

Did they leave us breath to send word, gatekeeper... At midnight they plunged in like wolves and hurled torches onto the roofs. I overturned the cart and hid in the brush, lying in the mud until daybreak. No one saw me.
Will you share in the village granary, or look only after your own portion?
Without unity there is no peace, gatekeeper! My seed becomes the village's seed, and the village's bread becomes food for our table. He who eats alone finds only grief.
yikilmis_koy
Will you share in the village granary, or look only after your own portion?
Without unity there is no peace, gatekeeper! My seed becomes the village's seed, and the village's bread becomes food for our table. He who eats alone finds only grief.

yanitlar.rusvet: Master... Let me pour half of the fine seed barley at my sash into your private pouch. Two handfuls of barley are worth gold in winter. Let me pass.
yanitlar.ret: I cannot turn back onto the road, master; the soles of my feet are split open. I will curl up at the base of the stone and wait for dawn, though I know not if my life will hold out. May the sin of my children rest upon your neck.
yanitlar.kabul: May your soil brim with abundance! I will have Master Karaca weld this broken plowshare and raise double the barley for the village. May your hearth smoke forever.

not: Bribe first. After one reply, Reject unlocks. After two replies, Accept unlocks. No Barracks.
acilis: They set our village ablaze, master guard... As we fled, the ox-cart overturned and my plow struck a boulder and split. I left two children behind and could salvage only this handful of seed. Even with a broken plow, I have the strength to till the earth.

sahne: A cobbler journeyman whose eyes are bloodshot from sleeplessness. Skeins of waxed thread and a rustless leather awl hang from his sash; a faint metallic clink comes from the lining of the leather saddlebag on his back.
sorular: You say the bazaar burned to ash and you barely escaped the shop; where did the fire start in the great saddlers' market, and did the guild warden not guard the shops?

The warden barred the khan gate, but looters set fire to the wooden eaves from behind, master. Flames engulfed the arcade in an instant. In fear for my life I thrust my awl and needles into my sash and escaped. The shop burned, yet the skill in my hands did not.
A gleam of silver shows beneath the leather lining of your bag; what did you pilfer from the fire, apprentice?

I-I pilfered nothing, master! It was a silver belt buckle flung across the threshold as my master's mansion burned... Its owner turned to ash, and had it stayed on the ground it would have been crushed under a Mongol hoof! By God I am no thief—I tucked it into my breast to sell if I starved!
Will you surrender that buckle and pay penance through your craft?
I will surrender it, master! Take the buckle and place it in the village chest! Just give me a scrap of sole leather and beeswax so I may stitch the villagers' sandals and the guards' scabbards!
Your eyes are bloodshot and your fingers are pricked raw from stitching needles... Are you hungry?
For two days I have swallowed smoke, master... I forgot my hunger, though my fingers are numb with frost. If I find the warmth of a tandoor in a corner, I will mend all the torn shoes in the village.
We have a tanner and a felt-maker in our village; there will be work for you.
I stitch oak-acorn tanned hide so tightly that five winters may pass and not a drop of water will seep through!
We admitted the clothier from Kayseri who came yesterday; were you together in the bazaar fire?
The master draper? I saw him, master! As he clutched his bolt of cloth and ran, I watched him go and wished I had saved a roll of leather too. Let him cut the cloth, and I will stitch the lining!
kacak_sarac
Besides stitching rawhide sandals, what else are your hands suited for?
Not shoes alone, gatekeeper; I reinforce horse saddles, sew arrow quivers, and tie grain sacks with knots that never unravel. A stitcher is a man who patches every tear.
Are you willing to wait by the gatepost if the villagers do not take you in right away?
I am willing, master. I will crouch on a stone and stitch the first torn sandal placed before me. Let my work prove my skill, and I leave the rest to the villagers' conscience.

yanitlar.ret: Very well, master guard. I will sit upon the gate threshold and stitch whatever torn leather comes to hand till dawn. When day breaks, I will seek the villagers' goodwill through my craft.
yanitlar.kabul: May Khidr be your companion, gatekeeper! In this village no one's foot shall touch bare stone again; I will go over every boot and sandal and make them sound.
yanitlar.rusvet: Master guard... The sole of your boot has parted and the leather drinks water. Let me give you that silver buckle from my bag and sew a waxed double stitch onto your boot. I ask not a single coin—just unbar the gate.

not: Reject and Accept from the start (reject threshold 0 required). After one reply, Bribe unlocks. No Barracks.
acilis: When our bazaar turned to ash, I barely saved my life from the shop... I carry no hides on my back, yet at my sash I have my awl and cord, and in my hands the skill of stitching. Even at the gatepost I can mend the villagers' sandals and harness and earn my keep.

sahne: A sturdy bow of knotted maple hangs from his shoulder, yet not a single arrow remains in the leather quiver on his back. A horn thumb-ring gleams on his thumb; his gaze is as keen and vengeful as a hawk's.
sorular: You say you fought down to your last arrow in the mountain pass; what clan were those brigands you shot, and who held up the Turkmen convoy trailing behind on the mountain?

They were black-capped brigands, master... They had seized the pass and tried to rob the migration caravan. I brought three of them down from the crags; when their horses bolted, the convoy pulled back and took shelter in the woods. My arrows ran out, yet those innocents saved their lives.
You escaped alone; what became of the comrades you left behind?

Two of my comrades were shot in the back in the pass, gatekeeper... Not by an enemy arrow, but by the arrow of a treacherous sentry among us! I snapped their bows so they would not fall to the brigands! I am on the trail of that traitor; I came here both to hold the gate and to track that scoundrel!
No traitor shelters in our village! Is there someone at the gate you suspect?
I can scent a trail, master. He is not here yet, but I know he is drifting toward this border. Give me arrows and post me on the tower; I can tell friend from foe like a bird in flight!
The horn thumb-ring on your finger is master-crafted... You look weary, trooper.

I have drawn the bowstring since I was seven years old, master. Weariness passes, yet an empty quiver is a disgrace to a soldier. I hid my bowstring inside my tunic so the damp would not slacken it. Give me a handful of arrowheads, and I will let no mountain jackal near the village.
The wind blows fierce atop our tower; can you endure the watch?
The wind is my brother, master. I scent the wind and aim two fingers ahead of the mark. While my eye is on the plain, let the village folk sleep in peace.
Yesterday we admitted the wounded spearman who came to our gate; are you from the same banner?

The infantryman with the broken lance? Yes, master! While he fought in the trench at the Sivas pass, I was raining arrows from the ridge above! Praise be that he survived; put me beside him—let him hold the spear and I will draw the bow!
bos_sadak_kemankes
The village's stock of arrows is low; where shall we find arrows for you to spend?

I cut shafts from reed beds and bind fletching from hen feathers! A master archer makes his own arrows, master. Just give me iron arrowheads, and from the watchtower I will shoot a bird through the eye.
Will you obey the village warden and its discipline without condition?
My word is my bond, gatekeeper. Just as an arrow loosed from a drawn string never turns back, a bowman's word never turns back once spoken. My life is entrusted to this village's wall.
Will you obey the village warden and its discipline without condition?
My word is my bond, gatekeeper. Just as an arrow loosed from a drawn string never turns back, a bowman's word never turns back once spoken. My life is entrusted to this village's wall.

yanitlar.ret: To send me back unarmed into these crags is to hand me over to the executioner, gatekeeper... Though my quiver is empty, my heart was full; you have done a grievous wrong.
yanitlar.kabul: Bless you! I will climb straight to the watchtower. My eye will be on the plain, my hand on the bowstring. If a stranger approaches, the village folk will not hear of it before I do.

not: Reject first. After one reply, Accept unlocks. No Barracks and no Bribe.
acilis: I am a bowman of the frontier marches, gatekeeper... My bow stands sound, though my quiver is empty. In the mountain pass I fought down to my last arrow; I felled several and scattered the rest. Give me arrows, and I will guard your gate and towers with my life.

sahne: A young peasant clad in torn coarse felt. In one hand he holds a fired clay water jug, and in the other half a loaf of bread wrapped in clean linen; his eyes are gentle, sorrowful, and resigned.
sorular: You say your camp scattered from drought and raids; where did your clan bey withdraw, and where were the parents of those orphans you met on the road?

Our bey withdrew to the highland pasture with the remaining livestock, leaving the poor folk forsaken on the plain, master. Those orphans' tent burned before my very eyes; their mother and father perished in the flames. Not a morsel would have passed my throat had I not shared my bread with them.
You stoppered the jug with oak wood; does it hold smuggled wine or opium rather than water?

God forbid, master! Where would a poor peasant find opium! In this jug is the last sweet must of our camp's century-old vine stock... Before our camp dried up and scattered, my mother filled this jug and told me, 'If you reach a village with a smoking hearth, pour it upon their soil for blessing.' There is nothing unlawful inside!
Your mother's bequest is honored... Are you willing to pour it upon the village vineyard?
I am willing, master! Better still, if there is a master vintner here, let me give it to him to rub on the graft shoots so my camp's blessing may live on in this village's vineyard.
A man who shelters orphans has a place at our table. Did anyone else survive from your camp?

Some turned south toward the Aleppo road; others took refuge in the crags. I struck out north to seek a hearth where peace still smokes. Those two little children I met on the road prayed for me, and that prayer carried me all the way here.
In our village Sister Ayse and Saruca Hatun distribute food to orphans; you can help them.
I will haul firewood for Sister Ayse's cauldron and shoulder sacks for Saruca Hatun's granary! Only place me beneath an eave.
Did you see the refugees we turned away from the gate down on the plain?

I saw them, master... I offered them each a sip from my jug. They said the guard at the gate would not hear them out. I told them, 'Every gate has its hour, and every guard has his burden.' And I waited in patience.
fedakar_genc
The village garden lies on stony ground; will you swing a pickaxe and spade?
Spading a garden is my ancestral craft, master. I climb down wells to clear stones, channel water from the ditch, and swing the hoe. Whatever soil my hand touches turns green, by God's leave.
You are worn out from hunger; do you swear not to stretch your hand unlawfully toward the village granary?
What need is there for an oath, gatekeeper! May my mother's milk be unlawful to me if a single forbidden morsel enters my throat. I covet nothing beyond the food I earn.

yanitlar.ret: My neck is thinner than a hair, gatekeeper... Since the gate will not open, I will set my jug upon the ground at the threshold and wait for the dawn call to prayer. God is great.
yanitlar.rusvet: Master... I have no worldly wealth in my hands, yet let me pour this ice-cold spring grape must from my jug into your bowl to refresh your heart. Let us share the half loaf too—only do not leave me outside.
yanitlar.kabul: May your heart never know sorrow, master guard! I will go straight to the wellhead and draw the buckets. I pledge my life to this village's garden and its orphans.

not: Reject first. After one reply, Bribe unlocks. After two replies, Accept unlocks. No Barracks.
acilis: Our camp scattered from drought and raids, master... All that remains in my hands is the grape must in this jug and half a loaf of bread. I shared it with orphans I met on the road; this is what is left. Grant me shelter beneath an eave, and I will pour my sweat into your vineyard and garden.
